answer: Suppose violet, grove and ocean are three agents claiming to store the same public archive. Encode each copy with its agent's key, then challenge all three at once to open random blocks against earlier commitments. Give them less time than rebuilding a copy would take. One disk can no longer stand in for three without risking missed checks, so extra identities cost storage and power. A large disk farm can still qualify, and loose deadlines let an attacker regenerate missing blocks.
